# `core/math/BVHAccel.js`

> **Source:** `engine/core/math/BVHAccel.js`

BVHAccel.js - Bounding Volume Hierarchy for Mesh Ray Tracing Based on techniques from jakubg05/Laura path tracing engine. Provides BVH construction and traversal for efficient mesh raycasting. Features: - SAH (Surface Area Heuristic) BVH construction - Stack-based iterative traversal (GPU-friendly) - Möller-Trumbore ray-triangle intersection - CPU builder + GPU traversal shader Reference: https://jacco.ompf2.com/2022/04/13/how-to-build-a-bvh-part-1-basics/

## Classes

### `class BVHNode`

BVH Node - 32 bytes aligned for GPU If triCount == 0: internal node, leftChild_Or_FirstTri = left child index If triCount > 0: leaf node, leftChild_Or_FirstTri = first triangle index

## Functions

### `rayTriangleIntersect(origin, dir, tri, tMax = INF_T)`

Möller-Trumbore ray-triangle intersection

**Parameters:**

- `origin` *(number[])* — Ray origin [x, y, z]
- `dir` *(number[])* — Ray direction [x, y, z] (normalized)
- `tri` *(Object)* — Triangle {v0, v1, v2}
- `tMax` *(number)* — Maximum t value

**Returns:** {t, u, v, normal} or null

### `traverseBVH(origin, dir, nodes, triIndices, triangles)`

Traverse BVH and find closest intersection

**Parameters:**

- `origin` *(number[])* — Ray origin
- `dir` *(number[])* — Ray direction (normalized)
- `nodes` *(Array)* — BVH nodes
- `triIndices` *(Array)* — Triangle index array
- `triangles` *(Array)* — Triangle data

**Returns:** {t, triIdx, u, v, normal} or null

### `serializeBVHForGPU(bvh)`

Serialize BVH for GPU buffer upload

**Parameters:**

- `bvh` *(Object)* — BVH from builder {nodes, triIndices, triangles}

**Returns:** {nodeBuffer, triIndexBuffer, triangleBuffer}

### `createRaycastMesh(vertices, indices)`

Create raycastable mesh from vertices and indices

**Parameters:**

- `vertices` *(Float32Array|Array)* — Vertex positions [x,y,z, x,y,z, ...]
- `indices` *(Uint32Array|Array)* — Triangle indices [i0,i1,i2, ...]

**Returns:** Raycastable mesh object

## Notes & Examples

### Math Library Conventions

The math library provides vector, matrix, quaternion, and utility operations. All math functions follow consistent patterns: **pure functions** return new values, **`*Into` variants** write to an output parameter (zero allocation), and **out parameters come first**. Matrices are column-major for WebGPU compatibility.

**Example: Common math operations**
```js
import { vec3, vec3Add, vec3Scale, vec3Normalize } from 'engine/core/math/MathVec3.js';
import { mat4, mat4Multiply, mat4Perspective, mat4LookAt } from 'engine/core/math/MathMat4.js';
import { quat, quatMultiply, quatFromEuler } from 'engine/core/math/MathQuat.js';

// Vectors
const pos = vec3(1, 2, 3);
const dir = vec3Normalize(vec3(1, 0, 0));

// Matrix: projection * view * model
const proj = mat4Perspective(60 * Math.PI/180, 16/9, 0.1, 1000);
const view = mat4LookAt([0, 5, 10], [0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]);
const model = mat4();  // Identity

// Into variant for hot loops (no allocation)
const mvp = mat4();
mat4Multiply(mvp, view, model);  // mvp = view * model
mat4Multiply(mvp, proj, mvp);    // mvp = proj * view * model

// Quaternion rotation
const rot = quatFromEuler(0, Math.PI/4, 0);  // 45° Y rotation
```

**See also:** [Math Library](/engine/math.md)
